en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-vinaya-sūtra*.

At that time, the Buddha was on Vulture Peak Mountain in Rājagṛha, together with immeasurable bodhisattvas, mantra-holding ṛṣis, the Great Sage Brahmā, the Earth Goddess, and others, expounding the dharma of mantras. At that time, Vajrapāṇi...
Rising from his seat, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and spoke these words:

“I now desire to expound the dhāraṇī-discipline; furthermore, I pray that the World-Honored One and all the great sages will each speak of its essentials, manifesting them for all those who recite and uphold dhāraṇīs.”
He further spoke these words:
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me leave to speak.
The Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"You possess great majestic virtue and harbor compassion within; being able to utter such words and delighting in the preaching of the sublime Dharma, you will surely bring great benefit.
We shall listen to what you say, and we, this entire assembly, shall all follow the Dharma as you have taught it."
Then Vajrapāṇi said:
"World-Honored One!

If there are sons or daughters of good family who wish to achieve the efficacy of the mantra-rites through recitation, such persons must first be diligent in the mantras they uphold. They must know how to make offerings to the Buddha’s stūpas and images, as well as to their own tutelary deity. Furthermore, according to their capacity, they should constantly perform offerings with an uninterrupted mind. Before the Triple Gem, they should confess their transgressions, make solemn vows and petitions, and dedicate this merit to all sentient beings, wishing that they may be freed from suffering."
Having spoken these words, he washed his hands, joined his palms, and knelt upon a mat of *kuśa* grass before the honored image, saying aloud:
"I pray only that the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, along with the mantra-holding deities and others, will look upon me, [Name], with compassion."

I now wish to experience the divine efficacy accomplished by this mantra-method; if I am able to accomplish the rite here, may the signs of success appear, and if I am unable to accomplish it, may the signs of failure likewise appear.

Having made this vow, one should recite with a sincere mind—either the root mantra or the heart-mantra and so forth—one hundred and eight times within the accomplished rite; then, one shall immediately fall asleep upon the seat.
If, within a dream, one makes offerings to the Buddha, the Dharma, teachers, monks, virtuous friends, or parents;
or sees oneself wearing pure white garments and adorning the body and head; or sees rivers, oceans, great mountains, pavilions, or halls;
or sees people giving one silken scarves; or mounts elephants, horses, oxen, and the like; or obtains swords, spears, battle-axes, bows, and arrows.
One may see copper wheels, hooks, or nooses; or see others bestowing upon one pure white garments, flower garlands, and necklaces;
or see oneself conversing with kind words with kings, ministers, or elders; or see a beautiful woman holding a banner, a parasol, or a flower vase;
or see one holding a spear or a trident in one’s own hand; or see oneself ascending a high lion throne.
Whether sitting on one’s own seat or another’s, or if one sees blood flowing from one’s head and body, or if such signs and circumstances as these appear,
one should know that one is now able to accomplish this dharma.

Or if, within a dream, one sees the painted images of honored deities or the statues of various spirits falling into decay and ruin; or sees one's parents grieving and weeping; or sees naked heretics; or sees oneself without clothing; or sees oneself being dragged away by those of evil karma, such as *caṇḍālas*; or sees oneself walking through filthy places; or sees great bodies of water drying up; or sees one's eating become excessive; or sees one's body, hands, or feet becoming soiled, foul-smelling, and stinking; or sees oneself fleeing in terror; or sees oneself pulling out one's own hair; or sees snakes, scorpions, rats, or wildcats; or sees oneself falling into a pit and sustaining injury—if one sees such signs and omens, it should be known that this person will encounter great obstacles and difficulties regarding this mantra-dharma, and its accomplishment will be hard to attain.

"If these sons of good family truly desire to joyfully receive, uphold, and achieve the efficacy [of this practice], they must apply themselves with diligent vigor without distraction; let them not give rise to thoughts of weariness or indolence. At every session, they must recite and maintain [the mantra] without fail or omission. They should always harbor a mind of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), remain far removed from sensual desire, and cultivate pure conduct (*brahmacarya*). Having bathed for cleanliness and become harmonious and supple, they should skillfully learn the methods and enter the *dhāraṇī* maṇḍala. To seek the great fruit, they must sever all heterodox speech and all talk of frivolous proliferation (*prapañca*). Out of compassion for the orphaned, the weak, the poor, and those young or old, they should assist and cherish them as if they were their own infants. They should know moderation in food and clothing, and those who practice together and are spiritual friends should mutually exhort one another. They should engender deep reverence and faith toward the Triple Gem, listen to the True Dharma like one parched with thirst seeking water, and constantly seek wisdom while attending to and observing virtuous friends."

Regarding the ritual procedures for the mantra altar, one must clearly understand the signs by which Vināyakas arise as obstacles and the methods for their expulsion; furthermore, one must skillfully study the rites of fire offering (*homa*), the methods for presenting food to non-human beings (*amanuṣya*), and the various mudrās and mantras for summoning and dispatching [deities].

Furthermore, one should know that as for the place of residence, one may dwell in a mountain valley facing a water’s edge or a ritual altar, or in a fine garden or forest where the vegetation is not withered, or beneath a single large tree, or within a stūpa containing the Buddha’s relics, or inside a pure monastery; in all such places, one may reside.

If there are places where there is danger from bandits, or where there are prostitutes, widows, caṇḍālas, wild beasts, or venomous snakes; as well as the homes of leather shoemakers, butchers, executioners, those who raise camels, donkeys, pigs, dogs, chickens, or hawks for hunting; and likewise places such as cemeteries or the dwellings of physicians and non-Buddhist practitioners—a practitioner of mantras should not reside in any such locations.

Furthermore, one must examine the place where one dwells; if there are no insects or ants in the water, and it is free from the falling of corpses, excrement, filth, and the like, yet possesses the foul vapors of green cliffs, it is likewise unfit for habitation.

One must distance oneself from [such places] and seek a superior location—one where sand, stones, flowing springs, and mountain pools abound and vegetation flourishes—only then may one reside there to engage in recitation and upholding [the teachings].

"When the exterior is pure, the interior shall likewise be upright and luminous. One must deeply renounce the mind of greed and desire; regarding all forms of anger and resentment, one should instead practice loving-kindness and patience, thereby subduing all afflictions."

Three times each day, enter a stūpa or a place for practice in the wilderness to confess and repent openly; rejoice in all meritorious virtues, dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and ensure that the aspiration to attain Buddhahood never leaves your mouth.

During both the first and last watches of the night, one should practice with diligence and contemplation, reciting the subtle and wondrous Mahāyāna sūtras, and receiving and upholding the rules for mantras and maṇḍalas, ensuring that they are never forgotten.

One should recite the mantras of the Great Wrathful Vajra Kings and others, giving rise to great joy and visualizing the forms of the Honored Ones as if they were present before one's eyes. With a mind that delights in cultivation and study, one should contemplate and recite the words of the mantras with a sincere heart, causing the eye of the mind to perceive impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and the lack of any solid reality, so as not to follow the realms of the five desires.

Regulate the breath so that it remains supple and does not become agitated; perform the ritual procedures with careful scrutiny. If you wish to rise and move, deliberate and steady your lifting of the feet; ensure that the recitation of the mantra’s phrases, the phonemes, and their characteristics are all clearly articulated.

If one should cough while correctly reciting the mantra, one must endure it; whether it occurs at the end, the middle, or more or less frequently, if there is any coughing, one must always begin the recitation again from the beginning.
“World-Honored One!
If mantra-practitioners and others are able to practice according to this dharma, before long they will attain great majestic power and efficacy.
All vināyakas and other obstructing spirits will be unable to create hindrances and will all flee far away.”

If, when a mantra-practitioner or others recite mantras, their speech is incorrect, syllables are omitted, their mouth becomes dry and parched, they are constantly clearing their throats, causing the sound of the mantra to be interrupted, or if their body is not pure—at such times, they will be taken advantage of by Vināyakas; the various devas and benevolent spirits will not provide protection, and they may encounter great illnesses or calamities, so that the rite fails to produce its efficacy.
Such unrighteous practices as these, the mantra-reciters and others should not perform.

With single-minded devotion, they should sit in the full lotus posture upon a mat of *kuśa* grass and recite the mantra with utmost sincerity. Internally harboring compassion, they should resolve their minds to remain free from distracting thoughts, thinking: "I perform this ritual for the sake of all sentient beings. They should continue reciting in one sitting until the body is no longer fatigued; thereafter, they may rise to walk in meditation, make offerings, read the scriptures, and praise and prostrate to the World-Honored One.
"In all times as previously described, one should act in this very manner.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"O Vajrapāṇi! You are able to speak thus, protecting and upholding those who recite mantras, and revealing to them the subtle and wondrous mantra discipline they require.
Then Vajrapāṇi spoke again as follows:
"I shall now explain the methods for making offerings to the original mantra-deity kings and others.

The practitioner of mantras must first bathe their body according to the dharma and remain free from distraction. Contemplating the original mantra-deities and others, they should prostrate themselves on the ground with all five limbs, pay homage, and give rise to great faith, saying:
'All that I seek in the Dharma is sustained by the majestic power and grace of the Great Deity.'"
Recite the mantra while giving rise to mental visualization. Facing south, form the Vajrapāśa mudrā or the Uṣṇīṣa mudrā with a mind of great wrath, and silently recite the Great Vajrapāśa mantra:
“Oṃ vajra-pāśa hili. If one forms the Uṣṇīṣa mudrā, then recite this mantra:
“Oṃ gagaṇa-māla hūṃ. Having completed the visualization toward the south, next visualize the west.
Mentally forming the Vajradhvaja-mudrā, silently recite the mantra with wrathful intensity and say:
"I now bind the boundary of the western direction.
The mantra is as follows:
"Oṃ talaṃkariṭha. Next, visualize the northern direction and form the Vajra-Crushing Mudrā.
Recite the mantra as before:
"Oṃ harivajrakarī maṭha. Next, visualize the eastern direction, form the Vajra-śikhara mudrā, recite the mantra as before, and say:
"I bind the boundary of the east."
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajraśikhari-maṭha. Having performed this rite, the boundary of the four directions is immediately established.
However, one must rise from one's seat, recollect the root mantra, and invoke the mantra-deities; holding an incense burner in hand, one burns incense as an offering.
Visualizing that I now rely upon the invocation of those of great majestic power and virtue, one prostrates with the body cast to the ground while recollecting the root mantra.
Taking pure water, one sprinkles it over the body and sits upright with the hands placed at the chest.
Recite silently while counting the beads; when you feel weary before reaching exhaustion, rise as you please to take incense and flowers for offering.
When wishing to exit the door, recite the mantra with single-minded concentration.
If there is any distraction, at that time all the *vināyaka* spirits and deities will conceive schemes to cause the mantra-practitioner’s mind to become disordered, thereby obstructing the rite.

If this is not successful, one should immediately manifest transformed flowers of various colors and various fragrances to cause the heart of the mantra-practitioner to be moved by desire and attachment.

However, he should not indulge in such pleasure; instead, he should rebuke [the manifestation] and depart, while constantly reciting and contemplating the original mantra-deities and so forth, never failing or forgetting them whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down.

“World-Honored One! This person is constantly followed by Vināyakas who seek an opportunity; if they do not act according to the Dharma, they will create obstacles and difficulties. However, if one practices in accordance with the Dharma, no such beings can find an opening. We Vajradharas, wielding our divine vajras, shall always provide protection so that the efficacy of the rite may be swiftly realized. If the practice is contrary to the Dharma and not in accord [with the teachings], we shall abandon them.”

Possessed by various māras, vināyakas, and spirits, or with wind entering the body, one frequently harbors anger and gives rise to stinginess, greed, and delusion; if these are not treated, they may even lead to death.
"If one later feels regret and acts in accordance with the Dharma, they will likewise be able to subdue all māras, evil spirits, and vināyakas.
The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is;
what you have said is not false. In this way, one should comply with the dhāraṇī method to achieve accomplishment."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat and spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!

Furthermore, if there are those who cherish their own lives and seek to realize and enter into the spiritual efficacy of the Dharma, those mantra-practitioners must all sever all evil deeds; they must not contemplate the physical beauty or the features of women’s bodies, nor, even if they see them naked, should they look back upon former objects of attachment or harbor thoughts of them. They should fix their minds on a single object, constantly mindful of the great majestic power of the Triple Gem, and abide always in the true mark (*dharmatā*). They should contemplate that all conditioned phenomena in the world are impermanent, suffering, empty, and non-self. With a single mind, they should dwell peacefully in the recitation of the fundamental mantra methods without allowing distraction, observing with upright integrity and refraining from grasping at delusive thoughts. Furthermore, they should recite the profound and subtle Mahāyāna sūtras, diligently make offerings to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and construct ten million (*koṭi*) stūpas and images so that no effort goes to waste.
"If one can practice in accordance with this, this son of good family will before long achieve great realization, and no ghosts or spirits will be able to create obstacles for him.
At that time, the Great Brahma Heaven King, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

I have constantly observed those who recite and uphold this dharma-gate seeking accomplishment, yet whose physical strength is weak, who suffer from excessive sleep, who do not eat or drink and whose bodies and heads are frail, who are indolent and lazy, afflicted by illness, prone to anger, and addicted to sensual desires; who give rise to improper thoughts regarding their own place of practice, who are insatiably greedy and always harbor doubts, and who, having already obtained the subtle and secret dharma, fail to practice it accordingly, instead seeking out other mantras and engaging in mutual conversation to debate right and wrong.
Again, he spoke these words:
"Which classes of people succeed in obtaining efficacy through the recitation of mantras?
Which mantras are capable of accomplishment?"
"Who else has their wishes fulfilled?
In which direction or location does recitation and upholding bring about accomplishment and efficacy?
"World-Honored One!"
Why do such people pass their time in vain?

Furthermore, there are others who earnestly seek to study and practice such mantra-dharmas; yet after a brief period of diligence, they give rise to regressive thoughts, violating the pure precepts of the Buddha to serve as administrators for the Saṃgha. I observe that they contemplate evil karma, forcibly engaging in actions they ought not to perform, and consuming food that they ought not to eat.

The World-Honored One is the excellent condition for all noble ones and the guide who opens the path for humans and devas; you reveal the causes of right action so that one may attain wondrous fruits. I only pray that out of compassion and for the benefit of humans and devas, you will explain this to me.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Brahmā, saying:
“Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon this well!

Great Brahmā, you should know that if there are those who wish to seek the study and upholding of dhāraṇīs, yet have not yet given rise to the great bodhicitta with a profound mind, still harbor doubts regarding the Mahāyāna, receive the root texts of the dhāraṇī methods without having received them from a teacher, whose words and phrases are disordered, who constantly see, hear, read, or recite subtle and secret teachings yet possess no understanding of them, who do not recite the dhāraṇīs or perform the rites according to the proper seasons, and whose dhāraṇī methods and maṇḍala rituals they have never clearly understood—”
What kind of person is this?

It is like one born from a mother’s womb who is devoid of both eyes; clinging to his perceptions, he wanders blindly through unrighteousness. He understands not a single method among the incantations, yet, because he is attached to the perverted self through ignorance, he utters words of folly, claiming that his wisdom clearly understands all phenomena.
"Mahābrahmā!

If this mantra-practitioner performs this rite of mantra while harboring such thoughts, there is a Vināyaka named Vajravikrama who will immediately create obstacles for that person, causing their body to be ill at ease and the mantra-rite to fail."
"Mahābrahmā!

If a mantra-practitioner, when bathing his body, does not form mudrās and recite mantras according to the ritual rules, fails to invoke the tutelary deity, and fails to sprinkle water [upon himself], he will be harmed by a Vināyaka named Tunga."

If a mantra practitioner is afflicted by the obstacles and harms of the Vighnas, his vital energy will become weak, he will suffer from excessive sleepiness, his thoughts regarding the performance of rituals will be clouded by doubt, he will be indolent and lack diligence, and he will be tormented by the suffering of illness.
For what reason?
It is simply because the mantra-practitioner lacks single-minded devotion, seeks much without satiety, and fails to engage in spiritual cultivation.
Great Brahmā!
If this is the case, what practice should be performed to eliminate [the obstacles]?

One who recites and upholds mantras should first seek out an ācārya who clearly understands the methods of mantra; having established the altar ritual, one must enter into it and learn and receive one seal from among the four seals.

Once the preceptor has conferred the empowerment, he should then, before a statue or image, recite the mantra one hundred and eight times over black sesame seeds and clarified butter, burning them in the fire; thus, all Vināyakas will be entirely dispelled.
Mahābrahmā!

Entering the maṇḍala and receiving the Dharma confers great power; yet, if one has not yet fully understood the dharmas maintained by mantras, lacks the bodhicitta, shows no reverence for the field of merit, and is ignorant of the vināyakas, one should not rashly perform the great rites, recite mantras, or make offerings.

Furthermore, there are some people who, having not yet entered the maṇḍala themselves, not yet made offerings to the ācārya, and not yet received the seal-dharmas (*mudrā-vidhi*), proceed to teach this secret dharma to others, saying:
"This mantra possesses such supernatural powers; one should employ this rite to bind, subdue, summon, and dispatch such spirits and deities."

Furthermore, he instructed him on the construction of altars, various mudrās, and so forth, commanding him to observe a vow of silence: "If you act in this manner, you shall laugh or weep; the mantra-deities likewise have such messengers."
"Mahābrahmā!

Because these people lack knowledge, although they act as teachers and recite the texts, they do not understand the profound and subtle Dharma-gates or the rules of ritual procedure; they merely initiate others by teaching and proclaiming that 'this is the Dharma.'"
Such a person is further possessed by a vināyaka named Riddhaṅgara, who causes many calamities and prevents the mind from attaining even momentary stability.
"Mahābrahmā!

If such obstacles and difficulties arise, one must further enter the Lotus Dharma-maṇḍala assembly and receive the initiation rites from an ācārya. One who is able to do so will have the Vināyakas removed."
"Mahābrahmā!

Within my Dharma, there are further classes of śramaṇas who, being ignorant of the subtle rules of the dhāraṇī methods, harbor thoughts of contempt toward their venerable teachers despite having maintained pure śīla. They disparage one another, seek honor within the monastery, and act with arrogance; some even resent the Buddha's teachings and slander the True Dharma."
Mahābrahmā!

You should know that such persons as these frivolously disparage my pure Dharma; consequently, they are possessed by a vināyaka named Nengzhang (The Obstructing One), who causes them to commit all manner of evils without ever feeling weariness or remorse.

If one wishes to dispel [these obstacles], one must construct ten million stupas and images; prostrate before the venerable master and solemnly receive the prohibitions and commitments; and likewise enter the Lotus Maṇḍala to receive empowerment. Only by doing so can that which is clung to be extinguished, and the dharmas for study, recitation, and retention will be easily accomplished.
At that time, the Earth Goddess Dṛḍhā emerged from the earth, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How should a mantra-practitioner protect the purity of body and mind?”
"What is walking meditation?
By what means may one know when it is appropriate to walk and when it is not?
World-Honored One!"
At what time and season must the mantra-practitioner recite the mantra?
How is one to know that it is the proper time for reciting the mantra?
We pray only that the Tathāgata, out of compassion, will explain this for us.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Earth Deity, saying:
"Listen well now to the rules for the practice that a mantra-reciter should follow.

If one wishes to receive and uphold any mantra-dharma, one must have deep reverence and faith in the heart, generating a sense of earnest gravity; one must abandon wrong views, unwholesome dharmas, and even frivolous laughter."
Reflecting deeply and forming this thought, one should practice four kinds of pure conduct. What are these four?
First is purity of body; second is purity of speech; third is purity of mind; and fourth is purity regarding food and water.
The conduct of body, speech, and mind constitutes internal purity.

As for the practitioner of external purity, when a mantra-reciter bathes his body and enters the water, he first puts on his bathing robe, recites this mantra while contemplating it, and rubs and massages his body.
The mantra is:
"Oṃ dūpe dūpe kārye dūpe prajñāpālite svāhā. Then, wash the body and head.
Having scrubbed one's feet with bricks or stones, one should take some earth and divide it into three portions. Taking one portion with the left hand, one recites this mantra:
"Oṃ bhuja-bara hūṃ. Reciting the mantra mentally, one washes the lower part of the body.
Next, take the second portion; reciting the mantra mentally, use it to wash the feet.

Having washed the hands until they are clean, next take the third portion and recite the mantra to wash the head. Then, reciting the aforementioned mantra, sprinkle water over the body. Next, fill both palms with pure water and again recite the aforementioned mantra to express one's fundamental resolve, saying:
"This water is offered to the deity of the root mantra."
Wearing new, clean robes, one should take fragrant flowers according to one's means to make offerings to all the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and all worthy sages, and openly confess:
"I now offer this body of mine to the Triple Gem."

"Relying on what has been explained above, one should perform the ritual and recite the mantra with true faith, sitting upright with a single-minded focus until one becomes weary. When one feels exhausted, one may rise as one pleases to practice walking meditation and beg for food and drink; having obtained food and drink, one should use this mantra to consecrate it before dividing it to eat."
The mantra is:

*Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām oṃ balandate tiṣṭha sma riṇi svāhā*. Having recited the mantra three times, first take a small portion and offer it to the deity of this mantra, and then partake of food oneself.

Having washed the alms bowl and purified the mouth, one should, as before, bathe and return to the ritual arena (*maṇḍala*). There, perform offerings, repentance, and the recitation of scriptures; then sit and chant mantras until one is no longer fatigued. When the body grows weary, one may rise as one pleases to practice the Way, continuing likewise until evening.
If you become weary while reciting the mantra, perform circumambulation and make offerings to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, prostrating and offering praise.

If you wish to sleep, lie on your right side and contemplate that the body is impermanent and without self, ultimately being suffering, empty, and impure—a mere assembly of skin and bone. With this contemplation, recite the mantra and enter sleep.
The mantra is:

"Oṃ vajraśāni hūṃ. If one recites this mantra, all evil dreams will be completely extinguished, and one will be protected by benevolent deities, swiftly attaining the signs of spiritual efficacy. Such are the rules for the timing and ritual procedures of pure conduct.
At that time, the Earth Deity again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
When a mantra-practitioner recites and upholds the Dharma teachings, how may one know through dreams whether the signs of the Dharma are auspicious or inauspicious?"
The Buddha addressed the Earth Deity, saying:

“If a mantra-practitioner or others who delight in receiving, upholding, reciting, and contemplating the dharma of mantras practice with diligence day and night without a mind of indolence or retreat, then even when that person is asleep, they shall see in their dreams a boy or girl beautifully adorned, or the appearance of their parents, brothers, or sisters; you should know that the mantra-deity is turning its gaze toward me.”
If you see men or women before you holding objects such as incense, flowers, food, drink, or fruit, you should know that the mantra deity has drawn near to you.
If you see yourself adorned in pure white garments, you should think: "The mantra deity is compassionately protecting me," and you must immediately apply yourself with diligent vigor.

If one dreams of the aforementioned men and women holding aloft high banners, streamers, parasols, necklaces, crowns, conch shells, swords, and so forth, one should know that the efficacy of the mantra practice is near at hand.
If one sees men or women before a śramaṇa making offerings to the Triple Gem, practicing giving, or staying within a flower grove, a monastery, or a stūpa, one should form this thought:
"I have now been received and protected by the mantra-deity."
If one sees [the Buddha] ascending a mountain, rising to a high pavilion or a lion throne, or wishing to leap into the void, one should form this thought:
"The time for my own dharma-verification is now very near."

If one sees him sitting upon a mountain peak, or on a lion throne, riding upon lions, white elephants, and the like; wearing a celestial crown, occupying the central position as the honored one, and being revered by all people—having seen these signs, it is a great manifestation of the Dharma.
Earth Deity, you should know that the characteristics and signs of such mantra-practitioners are as follows:

if, in a dream, they see butchers, executioners, *caṇḍālas*, naked heretics, or *nirgranthas*; or if they see themselves with disheveled hair like a son in mourning, naked, fleeing in terror, holding impure things in their hands, grasping cooked meat, fish, and the like, eating sesame dregs, falling into a deep pit, or being attacked by elephants and horses—then you should know that there are *vināyakas* known as Vajra-Angry-Ones who are creating these obstacles for them.

If one wishes to dispel [obstacles], one should perform the mandala rites, mudrās, and so forth as described above; furthermore, by reciting this mantra one hundred and eight times, one will immediately achieve protection of the body, be freed from hindrances and difficulties, naturally see dreams, and behold various auspicious signs.
The mantra is:
"Oṃ vajranarāhṇa-ma-tha-vañjaraṇa hūṃ phaṭ. Furthermore, O Earth Deity!

There is a *vināyaka* named Vīravikramaśiras. If he sees a mantra-practitioner intending to apply diligent effort to accomplish a mantra-rite, he will cause him to give rise to thoughts of advancing and retreating, prolonging the duration of the practice and making his body uneasy. He hopes that the practitioner will find a favorable location on a certain mountain to perform the rite; thus, being afflicted by this, the practitioner becomes indolent and ceases to be diligent.
Furthermore, if one asks others about a certain location and they reply,
"That is a good place; there are few difficulties," one's doubts increase further,
the mind becomes unsettled between two options, and one loses the original resolve.
How is it known that such obstacles and difficulties exist?

If a mantra-practitioner, despite reciting the dharma-mantras, sees in his sleep during dreams a man with his hands and body cut or damaged, hears words concerning transgressions and faults, or sees a stupa or temple falling into decay or ruin, or sees a magnificent object from which he is barred from entering, one should know that these are obstacles created by the Vināyakas.

If, upon suddenly seeing these various evil signs, one unintentionally gives rise to regression or indulgence of body and mind, and wishes to dispel them, one should smear the altar and make offerings, placing fine incense, flowers, fruits, flavors, and food and drink within the altar. Furthermore, take a new vessel, fill it with water, and place it in the center. Recite the aforementioned bathing mantra over the incense-water vessel one thousand and eight times. Using this water to bathe the body constitutes protection for oneself; only then can one scatter and eliminate the Vināyakas and other obstructors.
"Furthermore, O Earth Deity!

There is a Vināyaka also named Vajravikrama, who causes the mantrika’s physical strength and vigor to weaken. Upon hearing the sound of his mantra, [the Vināyaka] gives rise to aversion and suffering, headaches, and constant suspicion; he always follows his own nature, and even when exhorted by others, he instead gives rise to anger, arrogance, pride, and self-indulgence, showing no respect for superiors and disparaging all."

If one recognizes these signs of obstacles and hindrances, one must first receive and maintain the Great Vajracakra Seal, construct a mandala, and enter it. Furthermore, one should employ the Tathāgata-Uṣṇīṣa Dhāraṇī-mantra, as recited below, to consecrate scented water one hundred and eight times for the purpose of bathing the body; by doing so, one shall succeed in eliminating the Vināyakas.
The Tathāgata’s Uṣṇīṣa Dhāraṇī says:
"Namo Buddhāya, harauṣaṇi śa, dhāra, vajra-javariṇi, pravajaye, rāja-javariṇi, rā-pratijñe, sabhāra-hara, saṃgha-hara hahara, ni-kāriṇa-tama-mate, hūṃ phaṭ. And recite the six-syllable heart mantra:
"Oṃ rānta bandha svāhā. This mantra is foremost when recited frequently; the vināyakas shall then depart from afar.

Furthermore, there is a Vināyaka named Vajramusala, who causes people to lose their minds and become confused about their original nature; or he causes those who should be mindful during recitation and the like to give rise to contrary thoughts. Past deeds appear before them as if they were possessed by malevolent spirits, such that they lose their cognitive faculties, and no matter how many mantras they recite, they only give rise to distorted perceptions.
At that time, the mantra-deities will depart and one will see evil omens in dreams.

If one wishes to purify and eliminate such obstacles and difficulties, one must make a great vow, give rise to the bodhicitta, and pledge to extensively save sentient beings. For one day and one night, one should maintain the fast with a sincere mind according to the Dharma, observing the pure precepts, and recite the aforementioned Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mantra without limit as to the number of times. One should tie a mantra-cord from five-colored threads, further consecrate it seven times, and bind it upon the left arm; only by performing this rite can one successfully eliminate malevolent vināyakas and other obstructors.

"Furthermore, regarding the method for constructing the maṇḍala: the mantra-practitioner must first perform repentance and purify himself, generate the bodhicitta, and seek out an auspicious site. Having fasted for one day and one night and maintained the precepts, he should draw the interior of the maṇḍala using five colors. Within it, he should depict the Buddha seated in the full lotus posture using fragrant liquid; to the right, he should depict the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, his waist and hips wrapped in tiger skin, holding a jeweled staff in his right hand and a water pitcher in his left."
On the left, paint the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, holding a whisk in both hands.
Below him, paint the wrathful Cakrasaṃvara, who is Amṛtakuṇḍalī.
Below this, draw three flaming tridents; next, draw various ritual implements of the ground, such as axes, hooks, mallets, pestles, clubs, nooses, conch shells, and so forth, adorning the perimeter.

Below Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, one should paint the Mahāsattva Hārītī, Gaurī, Pāñcālikā, Mahāśvetā, and others; each should have their hair bound up, and their celestial crowns, garments, water flasks (*kuṇḍikā*), flowers, and fly-whisks should each be depicted according to their respective original rites.

One should paint the form of a single-crested rākṣasī, her teeth protruding from her mouth in a terrifying manner, wearing a human skull as a crown, seated upon a stone and entwined with snakes. She has four hands: the first right hand holds a battle-axe; the next holds a vajra; the first left hand holds a freshly severed head from which blood flows and drips; the next hand holds a vessel filled to the brim with blood. Her appearance is like that of an asura or a vināyaka.
Next, below that, paint the goddess Lambinī, whose body is clad in freshly flayed elephant hide.
At each of the four corners of the maṇḍala, place a vajra.
At the eastern gate of the maṇḍala, paint the deity Mahābhayānaka, along with a vajra and a mudrālañchita.
On the southern gate, paint a Great Vajra holding a battle-axe, who roars and terrifies the vināyakas; this is the deity Vajrapāṇi.
On the western gate, paint a lotus, with Tārānaṃduti in its center holding a torch in her hand.
On the north gate, paint Mahāvajraśikharanāman, here translated as "The Great Vajra Peak Attendant.
Once the painting is completed, one should prepare the various implements according to one's capacity and carry out the practice accordingly.
The colophon at the end of the *Vinaya-sūtra* from the Lingyun critical edition states:

"I respectfully present this transcribed copy of one fascicle of the *Guhyagarbha-vinaya-sūtra*. I humbly hope that future practitioners of the Secret [Mantra] will revere these pure precepts, so that all beings throughout the myriad worlds may be thoroughly moistened by the dharma-nectar."
Completed on the twenty-fourth day of the first *shang* month in the year of Jiazi of the Zhengxiang era,
at Yamimido-ji Temple in Kin-gun, Kawa Province, Great Japan. Recorded by the Bhikṣu Jōgen.
